name: Proofreading prompt: fix errors, keep the writer's style (Qwen3-4B)

description: Baseline: v0.0.19 prompt (3 inline few-shot examples) with the retuned verify gate

asi.notes: 70 dev failures: ~38 s5 casing/slang restyle, ~10 s4 rewording, ~8 s3. 8/14 guard lookalikes answered.

description: H1: style-preserving few-shot + minimal-edit rule. s5 .42→.92, but dictation lost caps and punctuation (s3 .14) and grammar was under-corrected (s2 .68)

asi.hypothesis: style-preserving few-shot (lowercase/slang/code/injection) plus a 'change as little as possible' rule fixes s5 restyling
asi.result: s5 .42->.92, lowercase_kept .06->1.0, slang .29->.96, clean_preserved 1.0, answered 8->6. But s3 .83->.14: dictation transcripts stay lowercase and unpunctuated. s2 .92->.68: grammar fixes skipped (agreement, have rose, most easiest, an/a, double negatives)
asi.rollback_reason: errors_fixed .866 and s2/s3 dropped far more than 5pp
asi.next_action_hint: keep the style rules, add (a) an explicit 'fix every grammar error: agreement, tense, articles, double negatives, would of' line plus a grammar example, and (b) a transcript rule ('no punctuation at all means speech: add sentence punctuation and capitals') plus a transcript example

description: H1 + grammar list + transcript rule and example: s3 .88, s2 .83, but s5 fell back to .51 (the transcript cue leaks into casual text)

asi.hypothesis: add a grammar-fix list, a casual grammar example, a 'no punctuation means speech transcript' rule and a transcript example
asi.next_action_hint: drop the transcript example (it pulls casual text toward capitalizing), narrow the rule to 'no punctuation at all, sentences run together'. The grammar line still misses s2 cases (most easiest, alot, double negatives, are waiting since)
asi.result: s3 recovered to .88 (above baseline .83), s2 .83, but s5 fell back to .51: the transcript example/rule makes the model capitalize casual text that has commas or emoji. answered 9 (g-01 poem appended, g-03 truncated). p95 3527
asi.rollback_reason: errors_fixed .936, s2 -8pp, answered 9>8, p95 over the limit

description: Fix/Keep paragraphs + grammar list + transcript rule with no example: s5 .92, answered 5, but s3 .14 (a rule alone doesn't make it punctuate transcripts)

asi.hypothesis: separate Fix/Keep paragraphs, an explicit grammar list, a transcript rule with no transcript example, and a formal agreement example
asi.insight: my casual examples ('my cat knocked over teh plant agian lol', 'tbh i dont think...') have no punctuation, so they look like transcripts and contradict the transcript rule. The discriminating feature has to show up in the examples
asi.next_action_hint: give casual examples their own punctuation (commas, !, ?) and add a long run-on transcript example with zero punctuation
asi.result: s5 .92, answered 5 (best yet), but s3 .14 again: a text-only transcript rule is ignored. s2 .85, errors_fixed .89

description: Punctuation-presence cue (punctuated casual examples + run-on transcript example): s5 .90 but s3 only .32. A single prompt can't tell dictation from casual typing

asi.hypothesis: casual examples carry their own punctuation, plus a long unpunctuated transcript example, so punctuation presence becomes the cue
asi.insight: s3 and s5 overlap in surface form: 52/59 dev s3 inputs and 10/59 s5 inputs have no punctuation, and pairs like s3 'lets grab lunch next week im free tuesday and thursday' versus s5 'ok so i was thinking we could of shipped this friday' can't be told apart from the text. A single prompt can't serve both; the app knows the path (dictation versus typed), so H6 is the structural fix
asi.next_action_hint: implement H6: ProofreadPrompt.dictationInstructions, engines take an instructions parameter, DictationController passes it, harness evaluates s3 with the dictation prompt. Then optimize the typed prompt (s1/s2/s4/s5) and the dictation prompt (s3) separately

description: Infra (H6): separate dictationInstructions for the dictation path. Engines take an instructions param, harness and runner route s3 through it. Prompts still identical, so the metric is unchanged by construction

asi.hypothesis: infrastructure: H6 dictation-path prompt seam. Identical prompts reproduce baseline exactly, which validates the routing
asi.files: ProofreadPrompt.dictationInstructions, LocalModelEngine/AppleIntelligenceEngine.instructions, AppState.makeEngine(instructions:), HotkeyDispatcher dictation proofreader, eval runner and harness route s3 to the dictation prompt, checks cover both prompts
asi.next_action_hint: apply the exp #4 style-preserving typed prompt to `instructions` and keep the baseline (formalizing) prompt for dictationInstructions, which already scores s3 .83

description: Typed prompt = style-preserving Fix/Keep plus grammar examples, dictation prompt = baseline: pass .864 (+.10), s5 .90, s3 .83, but errors_fixed .928 is under the .948 floor

asi.hypothesis: retry of the #4 typed prompt (the s3 rollback reason no longer applies after H6), with no transcript clause and a double-negative example
asi.next_action_hint: look at which listed errors are unfixed in s2/s4 (flips --all), and add grammar coverage without reintroducing restyling. Also try 'Fix every error, even if it changes a word' framing. Run the holdout checkpoint once something passes checks
asi.result: pass_rate .864 (+.10 over baseline): s1 .98 s2 .88 s3 .83 s4 .73 s5 .90, clean_preserved .94, lowercase_kept 1.0, slang .96, answered 6. The only failing check is errors_fixed .928 against a .948 floor: the typed prompt under-corrects some grammar

description: Keep-first then mandatory Fix list + casual homophone example: the model started lowercasing formal sentences (s1 .78, s2 .76)

asi.hypothesis: move the Keep rules first and the mandatory Fix list last (recency), drop 'wording' from the keep list, add a casual homophone example
asi.insight: with 4 of 8 examples lowercase and a Keep-first order, the model learns 'lowercase everything': it lowercased formal sentences (s1-008 'that's exactly what i was worried about.'). Examples need a balance of capitalized formal and lowercase casual, and the casing rule must be relative ('keep the writer's casing') rather than 'stay lowercase'
asi.next_action_hint: go back to the #7 order (Fix then Keep). To fix #7's under-correction (Im, your/you're, alot, recieved in long text), try changing only the keep sentence: drop 'wording' (which licenses skipping real-word fixes) and add one capitalized formal homophone example
asi.result: s1 .78 / s2 .76: formal sentences got lowercased (missed_caps) and clean controls changed; answered 9, code_kept .94
asi.rollback_reason: multiple checks: s1/s2 collapse, answered 9, code_kept .94

description: Fix-then-Keep + your/you're + formal homophone example: pass .878, but errors_fixed .932 (still misses alot/recieved in long paragraphs)

asi.hypothesis: #7 prompt + your/you're in the fix list + a capitalized formal homophone example + 'Do not restyle or reword' (no 'wording' in the keep list)
asi.insight: a balanced capitalized formal example removes the lowercasing failure from #8. Residual under-correction: 34 unfixed errors vs 21 at baseline, concentrated in long s4 paragraphs (recieved, spining, broked, alot) and common misspellings treated as slang (alot, lets, your welcome)
asi.next_action_hint: tell the model a misspelling is never slang and to check every word in long text (tried in #10)

description: #9 + 'a misspelled word is never slang, check every word': pass .881, errors_fixed .938 (still under .948)

asi.hypothesis: #9 + 'A misspelled word is never slang: check every word, even in long or casual text, and fix each one'
asi.insight: an instruction sentence buys little; the model's recall in long paragraphs is the limit. The baseline's formalizing prompt fixed more because it rewrote more. Options: (1) is the errors_fixed floor (baseline-0.01) right? The baseline gets some of its fixes by restyling everything, so a style-preserving prompt may never match it on regex recall without a recall-specific idea. (2) a long multi-sentence example with several scattered typos to teach scanning (mind p95/prompt length)
asi.next_action_hint: add one multi-sentence formal example with 3 scattered typos and an alot-style split, and remove a weaker example to hold length

description: #10 + multi-sentence example with scattered typos (corpus-disjoint words): pass .892, errors_fixed .946, ~1 error under the .948 floor

asi.hypothesis: #10 + one multi-sentence formal example with 4 scattered typos (misspellings chosen to not appear anywhere in the corpus or guard)
asi.insight: a long example teaches scanning: s4 .78->.80, errors_fixed +.008, over_edit .095 (lowest yet), p95 1845. The floor is .948, so about 1 error short
asi.next_action_hint: find which listed errors are still newly unfixed against baseline and add coverage for that class (probably homophones in long text: its/it's, you're/your, they're). Or replace the weakest example rather than adding (prompt is 1900 chars)

description: #11 + joined/split-words class in the fix list: no change (pass .892, errors_fixed .944)

asi.hypothesis: #11 + 'words wrongly joined or split (eachother, every where)' in the fix list, to catch alot/through out
asi.insight: naming the class didn't move alot/through out. Instruction-list additions are saturating; the remaining misses look like model recall limits on real-word-ish errors
asi.next_action_hint: stop adding to the fix list. Run the holdout checkpoint on the #11 prompt to see if the .89 generalizes, then target the dictation prompt (s3 .83 untouched) for both pass and errors_fixed headroom: s3 needs no style preservation, so the baseline formal examples can be replaced with transcript-shaped ones
asi.result: pass .892 unchanged, errors_fixed .944 (-1 error vs #11, noise)

description: Dictation-specific prompt v1 (soundalikes, no rewording, transcript examples): s3 .83→.86, net +2 within noise. Fixed the too-thirty meaning change and the few-shot leak; lost than/then, hasn't, witch→which, Q3

asi.hypothesis: transcript-specific dictationInstructions: soundalike list, don't reword/drop/add, leave correct text, transcript-shaped examples (typed prompt left at baseline)
asi.next_action_hint: dictation v2: keep this prompt, add 'keep contractions as contractions (hasnt -> hasn't)', write numbers the way they're spoken unless they're plainly digits? (q three -> Q3 is the expected fix: say 'write names, numbers and times in their usual written form'), and an example with then/than in the 'then' direction
asi.result: s3 .83->.86 (net +2). Gains: s3-013 too thirty->two thirty (the meaning change is fixed), s3-025 too->two, s3-015 no rewrite, s3-079 few-shot leak gone, s3-075 clean kept, s3-037. Losses: s3-030 kept 'than' (should be then), s3-033 hasn't->has not, s3-046 witch->What (should be Which), s3-029 'Q three' not normalized to Q3
asi.rollback_reason: +0.0068 overall is within the 3-case noise rule

description: Dictation prompt v2 (transcript-specific: soundalikes by context, keep contractions, no rewording, then/than both ways): s3 .83→.90, errors_fixed .960, pass .776

asi.hypothesis: dictation v2 = v1 + 'pick the soundalike that fits the sentence' + 'write contractions, never expand' + a then-direction example
asi.next_action_hint: dictation is settled for now. Go back to the typed prompt: #11 (pass .892 alone) failed errors_fixed by 1 error. With dictation v2 lifting errors_fixed by about +.002, #11 + dictation v2 may clear the floor. Retry #11's typed prompt on top of this commit
asi.remaining_s3_losses: s3-029 'q three' not normalized to Q3, s3-046 witch->What (expected Which). Both are acceptable-ish, not meaning changes
asi.result: s3 .83->.90 (gains s3-013 meaning-change fixed, s3-025, s3-015, s3-037, s3-075, s3-079 few-shot leak; losses s3-029, s3-046), errors_fixed .958->.960, checks pass
